user.title: Connect to TypeSafe
user.description: Paste an API key from your TypeSafe account. Home Assistant asks one short question to check that the key works.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-enter your API key
reauth_confirm.description: TypeSafe rejected the key currently stored. Paste a working one.

reconfigure.title: Replace your API key
reconfigure.description: Paste a different TypeSafe API key. Your questions and entities are kept.

error.cannot_connect: Home Assistant could not reach the TypeSafe API.

abort.already_configured: This API key is already set up.

init.title: Spending limits
init.description:
Input tokens are what you pay for, and question text counts as input. Set the budget past anything a working setup would use, so only a runaway reaches it. Zero means no limit.

The conversation agent sends anything it is unsure about to the fallback agent, whole and with nothing done first. Leave it empty and it will say it did not understand. Whole-house commands are refused unless you allow them, except for turning everything off, which is always allowed.

data.daily_token_budget: Daily input token budget (0 = no limit)
data.price_per_million: Price per million input tokens, in USD
data.min_confidence: Act only above this confidence (0 to 1)
data.allow_whole_home: Allow commands that name no room or device

daily_budget_exceeded.title: Jev stopped evaluating: daily budget reached
daily_budget_exceeded.description: The daily budget is {budget} input tokens and {used} have been used today, so no further questions are being asked. Answers keep their last value until tomorrow. Raise the budget in the integration options, evaluate contexts less often, or shorten your questions.

noul.name: Ask a yes/no question
noul.description: Ask whether something is true and get the probability of yes, from 0 to 1. Use one of these per label when several labels can be true at once.

state.name: State
state.description: The text to judge. Write a template and it is rendered before it is sent.

instructions.name: Question
instructions.description: Phrase it so that a high number means yes. A statement works as well as a question.

true_means.name: Yes means
true_means.description: Optional. What counts as a yes. Worth filling in when the boundary is subtle.

false_means.name: No means
false_means.description: Optional. What counts as a no.

threshold.name: Threshold
threshold.description: Where to draw the line for the is_true field in the response. The probability itself is always returned as well. A value near 0.5 means the model cannot tell, not that the answer is half true.

config_entry.name: API key
config_entry.description: Which configured key to ask with. Only needed when more than one is set up.

include_attributes.name: Include all attributes
include_attributes.description: Off by default. Sends every attribute of the picked entities, not just the value, unit, device class and area. A weather forecast or a media player artwork list runs to thousands of tokens, and you pay for them on every evaluation.

background.name: Background
background.description: Optional. Standing facts about how to read this, such as what a reading means for your particular device. It travels with the question rather than the readings, which measurably works better than putting it in the state. An object rather than a sentence keeps your own key names, and the model reads those keys.

choice.name: Pick one option
choice.description: Pick one option from your list, and get the probability of every option plus a confidence value.

instructions.name: Question
instructions.description: What the model is choosing between, in one sentence.

options.name: Options
options.description: Two to 255 options. Include a catch-all such as other when your list might not cover every input.

option_descriptions.name: Option descriptions
option_descriptions.description: Optional. A description per option, which sharpens the boundary between similar ones. Saying what an option excludes helps most.

instructions.description: One dimension per question. A question measuring three things at once produces a low confidence and a meaningless middle.

levels.name: Levels
levels.description: Two to 10 levels, lowest first. Describe a concrete situation for each, not a degree: Broken but there is a workaround beats Moderately severe. Each level is judged on its own, so comparative wording and numbers in the text do nothing.

ask.name: Ask several questions at once
ask.description: Ask any mix of question types about one piece of text, in a single request. Every question is judged independently against the same text and they run in parallel, so twenty questions take about as long as one.

questions.name: Questions
questions.description: Your own key for each question, then its type of noul, choice or score, its instructions, and criteria for choice and score. The keys are yours: they come back as the keys of the answers and the model never sees them.

nothing_to_judge.message: Nothing to judge: give this action some text, or pick the entities, devices or areas it should look at.

no_entry.message: No loaded Jev config entry to ask with. Add the integration first, or pick one under API key when more than one is set up.

missing_targets.message: These targets do not exist: {targets}. Asking about the rest would answer a different question from the one you wrote.

empty_target.message: That target holds no entities, so there would be nothing to judge.

too_many_entities.message: That target holds {count} entities and the limit is {limit}. Every entity is billed as input on every evaluation, so pick the ones the question turns on, or split it.

question_shape.message: Question {key} needs both 'type' and 'instructions'. Types are noul, choice and score.

wrong_answer_type.message: Asked a {question_type} question and got a {got} back, which the API should not do.

choice_options_out_of_range.message: A choice takes {min} to {max} options and this one has {count}.

score_levels_out_of_range.message: A score takes {min} to {max} levels, lowest first, and this one has {count}.

unreadable_answer.message: TypeSafe returned an answer of type {kind}, which this version cannot read. Update the integration.

common.not_understood: Sorry, I did not understand that.
common.whole_house: That would affect the whole house. Say which room or which device you mean.
common.which_kind: Which kind of thing do you mean? Say the lights, or the switches, or name a room.

data_description.name: Names the sensor this question creates.
data_description.instructions: Ask one thing. A question measuring two things at once answers near 0.5.
data_description.target: Pick entities, devices, areas or labels and their readings are sent for you. Leave empty if the note below is the whole state.
data_description.state: Text or a template, alone or alongside the readings.
data_description.background: What a reading means, for example that this machine draws under 5 W when idle. Measured: the same sentence is worth about twice as much here as in the state.
data_description.include_attributes: Off by default. A weather forecast runs to thousands of tokens on every evaluation.
data_description.scan_interval: Questions that look at the same thing on the same schedule are sent as one request, which costs tokens but almost no extra time.
data_description.true_means: Optional. Sharpens which way the answer points.
data_description.threshold: Leave empty for the probability sensor only.
data_description.advanced: A schedule, and what else to send. The defaults are fine for a first question.
data_description.trigger_entities: Evaluate when these change rather than on the clock. Debounced by 5 seconds.
